old: Setting Brahmins aside, the first to undertake explaining the Veda's meaning were the **Niruktakaras** — Yaska, author of the Nirukta. Yaska is reasonably well known even among those most familiar with ancient commentators, and subsequent commentators drew extensively on his work — though his own original text does not survive to us intact. Even so, his standing as the first commentator rests on the fact that his views and interpretations survive in fragments, drawn upon within many later commentaries. Having explained the meaning of a number of mantras in an ordered, systematic fashion, and having his own opinions preserved in this well-arranged way, calling him a Veda-commentator fits naturally — no other Vedanga author wrote so systematically. For this reason, Yaska's subject is not taken up here; this chapter gives brief life-histories of 16 commentators, beginning with Skandasvami.
new: Setting the Brahmanas aside, the first to attempt the meaning of the Veda were the Nirukta-writer Yaska. Since Yaska too cites many commentators earlier than himself, there may have been many commentators more ancient than he, but their works have not come down to us and are not likely to be found; so Yaska may be reckoned the first commentator. Since his Nirukta covers only some of the ṛks of the Rigveda, does not in many places explain the ṛks fully and in order, and also gives his own opinions, it cannot easily be called a Veda-commentary. Moreover, the Nirukta is counted as one of the Vedangas; so, without taking up Yaska here, this chapter gives brief life-histories of 16 commentators, beginning with Skandasvami.
